body: This needs a comment explaining why it resizes to this value, it looks odd

That's quite hacky, but I suppose it's fine until we add extra button navigation in other places.
You could add a comment though that ScriptEditor conflicts with this shorcut.
Any reason why not use `unhandled_input()` for the navigation? There would be no conflict with `set_process_input()` then.
Since you are doing resize, you could resize +1 more and set the last element instead of appending.

```suggestion
	tab_history_pos++;
```
The size is always pos + 1, no?

Can be a LocalVector
```suggestion
	LocalVector<int> tab_history;
```
I can do that, though existing codes seems to prefer this way, I tried to be consistent with it
I also set the grow mode to tight, let me know if that actually is a good idea

It would be better, but I tried to stay close to the existing implementation for Script Editor which does it just like this. Ideally inputs should be set as handled and the code moved to _unhandled_input, but I would suggest only doing so in both locations simultaneously, as otherwise priority can't be resolved properly anymore because of different input loops.
I added an explaining comment and improved the check to cover the case of the Script Editor being opened but not focussed, but yea this is not an ideal solution.
It's not, tight vector is for when the size is more or less constant. The history is growing very often.
